title: Weekly Reset
concept: About 40 minutes, five short parts: thank each other, check the load is fair, take on one friction point before it grows, then one ask each and one next step. Anything bigger (checking a Proof item, planning something fun, where you’re heading) waits for the Monthly Review. Maintenance, not a trial. Ours happens at home, on a Sunday.
whenToUse: Same day and time each week; also after travel or a hard stretch. Not for a fight: flooded? Pause + Return first.
steps: Appreciation (5 min) — each of you names one specific thing.
Check the load (15 min) — each of you says whether you’ve felt supported or alone, and whether the load feels fair. Once a month, this part is the Care Check-in.
One friction point (15 min) — each of you brings one small thing; agree a next step, not the whole fix.
Requests — each of you makes one specific ask for next week.
Next steps — agree one thing to try and when you’ll check back in. Requests and next steps share the last 5 minutes.
working: A sets forty minutes on the timer and B starts with an appreciation. It ends with the Thursday school run swapped and a check-in on Sunday. Neither of them is saving anything up for a row.
notWorking: B opens with Wednesday’s row; they skip the appreciation and set no timer. The check-in turns into round two.
activity: Book the next three weeks. Set a 40-minute timer; stop when it rings. Anything bigger waits for the Monthly Review. Use the Weekly Reset Agenda worksheet, or the button below.
